stories.headline: US designates PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist organizations, triggering Lula-Flávio political battle over sovereignty
stories.summary: The US State Department designated Brazil's two largest criminal organizations, the PCC and Comando Vermelho, as foreign terrorist organizations effective June 5, following Flávio Bolsonaro's meetings with Trump and Rubio in Washington. President Lula rejected the move as a sovereignty violation, calling Flávio a 'traitor to the homeland,' while the PL camp celebrated it as a victory; the dispute immediately became the central electoral flashpoint of the week, with PT filing a complaint to the PGR, government officials warning of financial and Pix system implications, ABIN and military officials raising sovereignty concerns, and Trump ally Jason Miller publicly mocking Lula.

stories.headline: Chamber approves 40-hour workweek constitutional amendment; Senate passage and Lula-Alcolumbre tensions follow
stories.summary: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies approved a constitutional amendment establishing a 40-hour, five-day workweek, ending the dominant 6x1 schedule. The vote strengthened Chamber President Hugo Motta's alliance with Lula, while Senate President Alcolumbre—already strained with the Planalto over the STF nomination—signaled interest in repairing the relationship to allow the PEC to advance before October elections.

stories.headline: Petrobras raises gasoline prices for first time in two years while government launches diesel subsidy to offset tax restoration
stories.summary: Petrobras announced a R$0.48/liter increase in gasoline distributor prices effective May 29—the first adjustment in nearly two years—driven by rising international crude prices from the Iran-Middle East conflict. Simultaneously, the Lula government issued an emergency decree authorizing a R$1.12/liter diesel subsidy and a new cashback mechanism, with Petrobras cutting diesel prices by R$0.3515/liter from June 1 to offset re-imposed PIS/Cofins taxes.

Lula accompanied Chambriard on regional visits and pressed Petrobras to prioritize domestic equipment suppliers. Separately, BNDES sold approximately R$3 billion in Petrobras shares to comply with Central Bank concentration rules after the stock's strong appreciation.

stories.headline: Lula government announces $75 million investment in BR-319 Amazon highway alongside environmental protection plan
stories.summary: The Lula administration announced a $75 million investment in the BR-319 highway connecting Manaus to southern Brazil, simultaneously unveiling an environmental protection plan to manage deforestation risk. Critics and opposition accused Lula of reversing prior environmental positions for electoral gain ahead of October elections, while environmentalists warned of accelerated Amazon deforestation.

stories.headline: Brazilian inflation exceeds central bank target ceiling for first time since October 2025; subsidized credit expansion draws scrutiny
stories.summary: Official data released in late May showed Brazil's 12-month inflation exceeding the upper bound of the Central Bank's 3% ± 1.5 percentage point target range, the first breach since October 2025. Analysts and Banco Central officials expressed concern that the Lula government's expanding subsidized credit lines—accelerated ahead of elections—were complicating the monetary easing cycle and keeping the Selic rate elevated.

stories.headline: Lula re-nominates Jorge Messias to STF after historic Senate rejection, signaling defiance of Alcolumbre
stories.summary: President Lula publicly confirmed he would re-submit Attorney General Jorge Messias for the open STF seat, following the first Senate rejection of a Supreme Court nominee since 1894 (42 votes against, 34 in favor). Lula attributed the rejection to political rather than technical reasons; analysts noted the re-nomination as part of broader Lula-Alcolumbre tensions and ongoing maneuvering within the court's ideological balance.

stories.headline: STF mediates R$6.5 billion rescue deal for BRB/Banco Master; PF signals interest in Vorcaro plea deal
stories.summary: The Federal District government and the Union reached a STF-mediated agreement to unblock a credit operation allowing BRB to receive up to R$6.5 billion through the FGC to absorb losses from toxic Banco Master assets estimated by the STF and PF at R$2.5 billion. The Polícia Federal separately signaled to STF minister André Mendonça that it would consider a new collaboration agreement with former Master banker Daniel Vorcaro starting from scratch.

stories.summary: President Lula launched Tela Brasil, a free public streaming service with over 555 national audiovisual productions, at an event in Rio de Janeiro, framing it as a 'cultural revolution' and defense of Brazilian sovereignty against foreign content. At the same event, Lula urged left-wing supporters to wear green and yellow during the World Cup to prevent the national colors from being 'taken by fascists'—a reference to the colors' association with Bolsonarismo since 2022.

Separately, a new instruction requires crypto asset companies to submit independent audit reports before receiving Central Bank authorization.

stories.headline: PGR charges nine people in STJ verdict-selling corruption scheme
stories.summary: The Attorney General's Office filed criminal charges with the STF against nine individuals accused of operating a scheme to sell fabricated rulings in the Superior Court of Justice (STJ), with investigators finding that false decisions had been inserted into the court's internal system.

articles.title: PGR denuncia ao STF nove pessoas por venda de sentenças no STJ

stories.headline: Lula faces legal risk over pre-election benefits package; PT legal team warns of TSE complications
stories.summary: PT-linked legal experts warned that President Lula's accelerating package of benefits and subsidies—including the new Gás do Povo program and Desenrola 2—could attract scrutiny from the Electoral Court (TSE) as potential electoral abuse of power, citing the Denarium precedent, even though the measures themselves are legal.

articles.title: Jurídico do PT vê dor de cabeça no TSE por pacote de bondades de Lula

stories.headline: Lula agribusiness outreach stalled by sector's demands for R$180 billion debt renegotiation
stories.summary: President Lula's ongoing effort to build political bridges with Brazil's powerful agribusiness sector faced resistance despite a series of credit line announcements, with rural producers pushing for renegotiation of up to R$180 billion in debts; Lula did not attend the Agrishow opening, sending VP Alckmin instead.

articles.title: Lula enfrenta jogo duro em negociação com o agronegócio

stories.headline: Brazilian Navy includes women in elite UN-evaluated quick reaction force for first time
stories.summary: The Brazilian Navy included women in an exercise of its Quick Reaction Force (QRF) as part of revalidation of the UN's highest peacekeeping readiness standard (Level 3 UNPCRS), marking a step in expanding women's operational roles within the armed forces.

articles.title: Marinha inclui mulheres em tropa de elite avaliada pela ONU

stories.headline: Lula undergoes radiotherapy after skin cancer removal; aides say health is stable
stories.summary: President Lula began a 15-session course of superficial radiotherapy on his scalp as complementary treatment following the removal of a skin cancer in April. Presidential aides said Lula is maintaining his agenda and the treatment does not affect his capacity to govern.

articles.title: Saúde de Lula preocupa? Veja o que diz um auxiliar do petista

stories.headline: Jair Bolsonaro completes two months under house arrest pending further medical evaluation
stories.summary: Former President Jair Bolsonaro, serving a 27-year prison sentence under STF minister Alexandre de Moraes' supervision, completed 60 days of house arrest as of mid-week. He will undergo a new medical evaluation at the end of 90 days (around June 27) to determine next steps.

articles.title: Bolsonaro completa dois meses em prisão domiciliar
